To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
any continuous mapping is approximated by Rumelhart, Hinton and Williams' multilayer networks with sigmoid hidden units and at least one hidden layers.

any continuous function can be approximated by a multilayer perceptron (MLP) network with at least one sigmoid hidden layer, and that the number of hidden units can be determined in terms of the desired accuracy of the approximation.
any continuous mapping on a compact subset of Rn can be approximated by neural networks with one hidden layer of sigmoid units, and that the same is true with two hidden layers.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

any continuous mapping is approximately realizable by a multilayer neural network with a single hidden layer and that any continuous mapping with bounded variation is approximately realizable with a finite hidden layer.

any continuous mapping on a compact subset of the n-dimensional real vector space Rn can be approximately realized (in the sense of uniform convergence) by Rumelhart-Hinton-Williams' neural networks with one or more hidden layers.
any continuous mapping from Rm to Rn (n > 1) can be realized by neural networks with at most 2n-1 layers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Rumelhart-Hinton-Williams' neural network can approximate any continuous mapping.
any continuous mapping on the compact set can be approximated by a neural network with at most two hidden layers.

the Rumelhart-Hinton-Williams model is a universal approximator of continuous functions and the number of hidden units required for the approximation is at most linearly related to the number of variables.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the number of hidden layers is a more relevant parameter than the number of neurons per layer.

the number of hidden neurons required for the approximation of a continuous mapping is not bounded from above by a constant depending only on the dimension of the space on which the continuous mapping is defined.
we have provided a proof of the universal approximation property of multilayer neural nets with sigmoid output functions.
